title: Joining tables: keys, cardinality and orphan records

videos.script: A join is the moment two files meet. Every analysis in this course ends in one. {{meet}} And a join never complains. Give it a key that repeats, and it copies rows. Give it a key with no partner, and it drops them, or leaves holes. {{silent}} Both happen in this company's files. Three products are listed twice in the catalogue. Join the order lines to it, and revenue grows by more than a hundred and sixty-seven thousand reais. Nobody sold anything. {{fanout}} Two product codes are not in the catalogue at all. An inner join throws their lines away, and more than forty thousand reais of sales go with them. {{dropped}} And two hundred and forty-six orders belong to customers the CRM does not have. Some joined after the export. Some asked to be forgotten. {{orphans}} So the rule for this lesson is short. Before a join, check the key. After a join, count the rows. {{rule}} A join that says how many rows went in, came out and found nothing is a join you can trust. {{end}}
